props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · the finished shine · scripted clock
props.title: A Line as a Test

B01.capture_spec: C01: Lab blob sprite (teal test sprite, scale to fit), lab-shaders/11-shine-clock.gdshader (TIME-driven, angle 35, thickness 0.1 as in the file); 12 s at 30 fps, Forward+, offline fixed tick; the sweep period is 2 s so the 12 s clip loops seamlessly; no input.
B01.visual_intent: Act title 'A Line as a Test' (serif 40) top-left. A real Godot render in a framed window on the cream stage: the teal test sprite with a white diagonal glint that slides across it from upper left to lower right, rests for a moment off the sprite, and repeats. Label: 'the finished shine'.
B01.motion_claim: The white band sweeps across the sprite and stays inside its outline.

show.event: sprite, window labelled, title on the card

B01.runner_up: manim drawing of a stripe crossing a blob
B01.why: A real render is the honest picture of the goal; a drawing would only claim it.

B02.visual_intent: Axes on the cream stage with a warm-grey line y = m x + b crossing the vertical axis above the origin, a terracotta dot marking b. A right triangle (one step across, m up) rides along the line under the label 'slope m: up per step across'. Then the line slides down until it passes through the origin: the b dot lands on 0 and the label becomes 'y = m x'.
B02.motion_claim: The slope triangle rides along the line, then b shrinks to zero as the line settles through the middle.

show.event: b dot ringed: its starting height
line slides to the middle; b = 0

B02.why: A rise-over-run triangle that moves along the line is the meaning of slope; a table of two terms would only name them.

B03.visual_intent: A square with corner labels (0, 0) at the top left and (1, 1) at the bottom right and its second axis pointing down (shader_kit uv_square). A terracotta dot sits at the top-left corner. The labels morph to -1, 0 and 1 and the dot glides to the middle; the formula 'p = UV × 2 − 1' appears under the square.
B03.motion_claim: The zero moves from the corner to the middle of the square.

show.event: UV square, dot at the corner
labels morph, dot glides to the middle (settled by 50 %)

B03.runner_up: ShaderLab with the line `vec2 p = UV * 2.0 - 1.0;` over a gradient
B03.why: Moving the zero is a change of coordinate system; Manim shows the labels and the dot move, a gradient would not.

B04.visual_intent: The centered square with its vertical axis pointing down (+1 at the bottom). A terracotta dot sits in the upper right labelled (0.5, -0.5). The vertical axis flips to point up and the dot's label becomes (0.5, 0.5) while the dot stays where it is on screen; a short warm-grey line y = 0.5 x then draws, climbing to the right, under the label 'p.y = -p.y'.
B04.motion_claim: The vertical axis flips and the dot's second number changes sign while the dot does not move.

show.event: square, y pointing down, dot labelled (0.5, -0.5)

B04.runner_up: ShaderLab showing the signed map upside down then upright
B04.why: A relabelling of the same dot on the same screen is the claim; only a drawing can hold the dot still while the numbers change.

B05.visual_intent: Left: the equation 'y = m x'. The 'm x' term travels across the equals sign and the equation becomes 'y − m x = 0', captioned 'the test'. Right: the square with the line m = 0.5 and a terracotta dot riding along it, labelled '0'; then a second dot off the line reads +0.6.
B05.motion_claim: A term crosses the equals sign while a dot rides the line with the value 0 on it.

show.event: y = m x, line and dot
m x crosses to the left side
the dot on the line reads 0
a second dot off the line reads +0.6

B05.runner_up: LectureCodeTrace of the single line y - m * x
B05.why: An equation that rearranges itself is a Transform; the term visibly changing sides is the step the voice names.

B06.visual_intent: The test square with the line m = 0.5. Three terracotta dots land at across = 0.4: on the line (label 0), above it (label +0.6) and below it (label -0.6). Warm-grey dashed vertical connectors then run from the two outer dots to the line, labelled 'straight up' and 'straight down', each 0.6 long.
B06.motion_claim: Dots land one at a time with their numbers; dashed verticals then measure the gap straight up and down.
B06.why: Exact arithmetic with vertical gaps drawn is the claim, and the gaps set up the distance argument later.

B07.visual_intent: The same square: the line m = 0.5 and a warm-grey dashed parallel line through the 'above' dot. A terracotta dot slides along the parallel line while its label stays '+0.6'. Then three parallel warm-grey lines appear labelled -0.6, 0 and +0.6.
B07.motion_claim: The dot moves along the parallel line and its number does not change.
B07.runner_up: ShaderLab signed map with a moving probe
B07.why: A number that stays put while a dot moves is only visible in a drawing; the shader picture comes next.

cues.label: shader_type canvas_item: the first line says this shader is for 2D drawing
fragment(): runs once for each pixel the shape covers; sets its color

props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · slope 0.5 · the card is a square sprite
props.caption: vector: a bundle of two to four numbers (vec2, vec4) · COLOR: the color of the pixel being drawn

B08.capture_spec: C02: Lab card, lab-shaders/01-signed-test.gdshader, slope 0.5, still PNG (640 x 360 frame, card 288 px centred). Probes: p = (0.40, 0.80) reads +0.593, (0.40, 0.20) reads +0.005, (0.40, -0.40) reads -0.603.
B08.visual_intent: Code card at left (the ten-line shader) whose first two lines carry one-line labels ('shader_type canvas_item: the first line says this shader is for 2D drawing', 'fragment(): runs once for each pixel the shape covers; sets its color'); at right a real Godot window with a square card showing the signed test: warm at the upper left, cool at the lower right, a grey strip between. Three readouts land on the card at the three points from the drawing: +0.6, 0 and −0.6.
B08.motion_claim: Readouts land on the warm, cool and grey regions in the order the voice names them.
B08.why: The same three numbers from the drawing, now computed by every pixel, side by side with the code that does it.

props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · slope swept by script

B09.capture_spec: C03: Lab card, 01-signed-test, slope 0 to 1.5 linearly over the clip (6 s), Forward+; slope is 1 at 67 percent of the clip.
B09.visual_intent: Code card at left with the uniform line highlighted; at right a real Godot card whose warm and cool halves pivot around the middle as slope sweeps from 0 to 1.5: flat at 0, a diagonal at 1.
B09.motion_claim: The grey strip rotates about the centre as the slope grows.
B09.runner_up: manim line pivoting about the origin
B09.why: The real picture pivoting is stronger than a drawing of it, and it is the same shader the viewer just read.
